facts.statement: The genus Lithoptila was named by Bourdon in 2005.
The species described within the genus is Lithoptila abdounensis.
Lithoptila abdounensis is a distant relative of modern tropicbirds.
facts.quote: It is a distant relative of the tropicbirds.

facts.statement: Lithoptila abdounensis was an extinct seabird belonging to the family Prophaethontidae that lived during the Palaeogene period.
facts.quote: Lithoptila abdounensis is an extinct species of prophaethontid seabird that lived during the Palaeogene period.

facts.statement: Fossils of L. abdounensis have been found in Morocco in strata dating to the Late Palaeocene and Early Eocene.
facts.quote: L. abdounensis lived in Morocco, its fossils having been found in strata dating to both the Late Palaeocene and Early Eocene.

facts.statement: The genus Lithoptila belongs to the parent group Prophaethontidae.
Lithoptila is classified within the family Prophaethontidae.
The genus Lithoptila lived between 61.66 and 48.07 million years ago, from the Selandian to the Ypresian.
facts.quote: Time range: Selandian to Ypresian (61.66 to 48.07 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Lithoptila is classified in the class Aves.
